I gave a number based on Levels and said I was seeing around 500 for this role. The recruiter was fine with it and didn't push back. In hindsight I probably should not have anchored that early, but that is how the conversation went.

Overview

My first technical was a 45 minute CodeSignal on a TTL cache. It was not very LeetCode-y. I wrote the basic solution, and then most of the round turned into follow-up discussion about tradeoffs, eviction, and where the implementation breaks.

Question types asked

[Coding](https://www.aced.io/questions?type=coding) [Technical](https://www.aced.io/questions?type=technical)

Specific questions asked

[Build a TTL cache.](https://www.aced.io/questions/6299)

What happens if you keep everything in memory?

You're evicting the cache lazily. What happens if you don't evict?

What are some ways to get around that?

I wrote a straightforward TTL cache in JavaScript, then we talked through the gotchas. I said if I keep everything in memory and never really evict, the cache just keeps growing. For lazy eviction, the same issue shows up if expired entries are never cleaned up. I suggested regular compaction or cleanup on a cadence. The vibe was less, can you grind code, and more, do you understand the failure modes of something you'd actually build.

Overview

The coding round in the onsite was the one that felt the least domain-specific. I got a tree traversal problem built around an org chart, and it honestly caught me off guard because I expected something more practical. The interviewer helped me quite a bit, so it ended up feeling collaborative.
